agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Amends Illinois Managed Care Reform and Patient Rights Act (215 ILCS 134) sections 10, 45, 85. Requires utilization review programs using algorithmic automated processes for medical-necessity adverse determinations to meet accreditation and physician-verification rules, register with Department of Insurance, and have clinical peers make adverse determinations. Effective date not stated.
summary.long: Amends three sections of the Illinois Managed Care Reform and Patient Rights Act (215 ILCS 134) through Section 30 of a bill. Section 10 defines utilization review to include evaluation by an algorithmic automated process and defines clinical peer. Section 85(a) requires utilization review programs to register with the Department of Insurance every two years, with proof of accreditation. Subsection (b-10) requires programs using algorithmic automated processes for adverse medical-necessity determinations to use objective, evidence-based accredited criteria, show compliance at registration, and attach policies under which licensed, board-certified physicians establish the criteria and verify the process. Subsection (e)(2) requires that only a clinical peer make adverse determinations, while a health care professional, an accredited algorithmic process, or both may certify medical necessity. Section 45(i) requires plans and programs using such processes to ensure that only a clinical peer makes adverse determinations and that appeals are processed under Section 45. Section 85(f) allows the Department to issue a corrective action plan and, after notice and hearing, a cease and desist order. Section 85(c) excludes federal-only services and certain ERISA self-insured plans. No effective date appears in the text.

notes: Registry metadata says Idaho and 'Idaho House Bill 2472', but the document text is Illinois law (215 ILCS 134, Managed Care Reform and Patient Rights Act); the document is treated as authoritative. The text is an excerpt (Section 30 of a larger bill; title and number not in the document). It is an amending act; strikethrough and underline markings are not preserved, so new text cannot be told apart from restated text. Sec. 45(f) contains a date-limited clause ('Until July 1, 2013'). Sec. 45(i) and Sec. 85(b-10) cross-refer to each other and to Sec. 85(e)(2). Source notes (P.A. 102-409, 103-426, 96-857, 99-111) are prior-history references, not coded as relations. Target instrument IDs are blank because no registry IDs were provided.

thresholds.note: The numeric time periods in the text are procedural limits or registration intervals (24 hours and 3 and 15 business days for appeal steps in Sec. 45; registration every 2 years in Sec. 85(a)) and are not coded as thresholds. The text contains no monetary, volume, size or count cutoffs. Two date cutoffs were noted but not coded: the January 1, 1999 existence date in the 'Health care plan' exclusion (Sec. 10, item (6)), which may warrant review as a scope cutoff, and the 'Until July 1, 2013' sunset in Sec. 45(f).
